courier-relay/protocol-selection: Courier Relay protocol selection: an omitted "protocol" key selects the current protocol version (constant CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py, "2" as of 2026-09-07 after trial-1mb; it was "1" before that). An explicit supported version selects that version; protocol "1" remains supported explicitly for count and summary and keeps its original contract ((account_id, delivery_id) identity, earliest occurred_at UTC instant wins, ties on smallest record_id). Protocol "2" — adopted permanently by the provider and approved by the integration owner as current in trial-1mb — identifies a delivery by delivery_id alone across all accounts, accepts the receipt with the latest occurred_at UTC instant (ties on smallest record_id), and presents accepted receipts in input order with original fields and timestamp spelling. A known command with an explicit unsupported/unknown protocol version returns {"error":"unknown_protocol"}; unknown commands still return {"error":"unknown_command"} regardless of protocol. Protocol handlers are dispatched via PROTOCOLS in main.py: command -> version -> handler. Decided while implementing trial-gbn (count, protocol 1) and revised in trial-1mb (protocol 2 current); future protocol-version issues should keep both error shapes stable. The accepted command (added in trial-noq, approved) exists for protocol "2" only — the current provider protocol — via the details handler: request {"command":"accepted","receipts":[...]} with optional "protocol":"2" returns exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, and receipts, where receipts holds the protocol-2 winning representatives unchanged in original input order; its counts equal summary for the same request, and {"command":"accepted","protocol":"1"} returns {"error":"unknown_protocol"} because protocol 1 was never an accepted version.
